class.name: CbList
class.brief_description: A row per player or item, with no code: its first child is the row, copied for every entry. A scoreboard, a team list, what a player carries.
class.description: Design one row as this node's child: any Control (an [HBoxContainer] of labels, a panel with an icon and a bar), built from ordinary nodes and the HUD nodes. In the game that child is hidden and a copy of it is shown for every entry of the list, in order, laid out as a [BoxContainer] does (down, or across with [member BoxContainer.vertical] off). The HUD nodes inside a row read [b]that row's entity[/b] instead of the local player: a [CbFieldLabel] with [code]{name}[/code] and [code]{combat.kills}[/code] shows that player's name and kills, a [CbFieldBinding] fills a bar with that player's health. In a row's conditions, [code]is_local[/code] is true on the viewer's own row, and [code]{rank}[/code] in a format is the row's place in the list, from 1. What is listed is the server's: who is in the world, and the fields its mods set on them. The list only decides which of them to show ([member where]), in which order ([member sort_by]) and how many ([member max_rows]). A list inside a row lists for that row's entity: [constant OF_HELD_ITEMS] under a player's row is what that player carries. Headers are not part of it: put plain labels above it. To show it only while a key is held, put a [CbKey] next to it.

method.name: get_entries
method.description: The entities it lists now, in order.

members.member: For items: only this kind ([code]pistol.gun[/code]). Empty: any.
Expressions on an entry, all of which must hold for it to be listed: [code]team.id == 1[/code], [code]not combat.dead[/code], [code]not is_local[/code].
An expression over an entry's fields that orders the rows: [code]deathmatch.score[/code], [code]combat.kills - combat.deaths[/code]. Empty: the world's order. Entries that tie keep their order.
At most this many rows (the first ones, after sorting). 0: all. A top three is 3.
Expressions on the list's own subject (the local player, or the row the list is in) that must hold for the list to be shown at all.
For a list of events: the mod event it lists ([code]combat.killed[/code]).
For a list of events: how long an event's row stays.
For a list of events: what [code]{a}[/code] or [code]{b}[/code] says when the event has no such entity (a fall: nobody did it).

constants.constant: Every item in the world, lying or carried. [code]{name}[/code] is its display name.
The items its subject carries: the local player's, or those of the player whose row the list is in.

The slots of its subject (a player), in their order, empty ones too. A row is for the item in its slot ([code]{name}[/code] is what that is called; nothing, for an empty slot), and the slot itself is in the row's own names: [code]slot.number[/code] (from 1), [code]slot.selected[/code], [code]slot.empty[/code], in conditions and as [code]{slot.number}[/code] in a format. They are read from the simulation's slots, so a row follows the player's hands on the tick of the key.

A row per [member event] that happened, the newest last, each for [member seconds]; with [member max_rows], the newest that fit. A row is about the event's first entity. Its names: [code]{a}[/code] and [code]{b}[/code] are what the event's two entities are called, [code]{event.value}[/code] its number, and [code]event.a[/code] / [code]event.b[/code] their ids, for conditions. A kill feed is this with one [CbFieldLabel] as its row: [code]{a} > {b}[/code].
